decisions.reason: As an adjacent multi-model supplement range with relatively low carrying costs, it still offers option value for portfolio expansion and pharmacy-channel learning.
This skin and hair supplement is close to the firm's consumer-health business and inexpensive to keep, so management would likely continue it unless sales had clearly disappointed.
Joint-health supplements fit the firm's broadening portfolio and can remain on the market as a low-cost option while demand potential continues to play out.
The immune supplement is a low-cost adjacent product with still-plausible upside, so the option to stay in this niche is worth preserving.

The earlier quality-related problem, combined with higher regulatory and reputational carrying costs for a more distant generic product, makes continued commitment less attractive than reallocating resources.
Although more distant and costlier to support than supplements, the OTC migraine product still has unresolved market potential and no clear negative signal that would justify immediate withdrawal.
